thread:
ashok: Heads up — security asked whether our export for privileged routing changes should include resolved actor emails or stick to hashed IDs. They need it for investigations but we also have PII rules.

maria: For hosted exports we can't ship raw emails by default. Can we gate full actor resolution behind an enterprise export flag + legal approval? :thinking_face:

ida: FWIW security said they often need 'who exactly made the change' when a policy misroute breaks a customer. Hashes slow down investigations.

jordan: Proposal: include actor_hash always, and an optional actor_email field only in Dedicated/Private exports or when export request includes `reveal_actors: true` plus an audit-approval token. That keeps hosted default safe.

sam: +1, but we need to think about rollover: if actor_email is optional we must also include actor_type and actor_role so reviewers know if it's a service account or human. Otherwise it's unclear.

ashok: Good call. Add these minimal fields: `actor_hash`, `actor_type`, `actor_role`, `actor_email` (nullable). Also `schema_version` on each line. Backwards-compatible.

maria: Also debating pre_vs_post snapshots vs diff-only. Security wants full context but NDJSON with full object every time explodes size. Any middle ground?

ida: We can include `change_delta` + `compact_snapshot` for small objects (like routing policy fields), and only include full `before`/`after` for large config changes when `full_snapshot=true` is requested.

jordan: To keep exports searchable, include `affected_paths` list (strings) that reference JSON paths changed. That helps SIEM consumers without full payloads.

sam: Architects will want schema examples. Quick sample NDJSON line for a privileged routing policy change: 

```
{"schema_version":"1","timestamp":"2024-11-20T18:12:03Z","event_type":"routing_policy.update","tenant_id":"acct_123","resource_id":"policy_x97","actor_hash":"sha256:abcd...","actor_type":"user","actor_role":"admin","actor_email":null,"affected_paths":["/rules/0/priority","/fallback_route"],"change_delta":{"/rules/0/priority":{"old":50,"new":10},"/fallback_route":{"old":"region-a","new":"region-b"}},"export_context":{"export_id":"exp_678","requester":"sec_team","approved_by":"legal_amy"}}
```

maria: Nice. For approved exports we would replace `actor_email` with the real email string. Need encryption-at-rest and access logs for export blobs.

security-bot: Note: compliance alert — any export with `actor_email` populated must be logged with a justification string and retention extended to 7 years per policy C-7.

ida: Another operational ask: can we stream exports (NDJSON) with backpressure and resume tokens? Security wants to avoid snapshotting big tenants.

jordan: We already have chunked streaming for metrics exports. Reuse the same pattern: token in response header `X-Export-Resume-Token`. Support `since_event_id` param to resume.

sam: UX: in Console we should show a small "exportable audit" badge on policy change display, with a one-click "Export this change" that opens prefilled export modal (scoped to the single policy + time window). That reduces guardrail mistakes.

maria: +1. Also add a console-level note: "Exports including actor emails require approval" with an inline link to request approval. Keep the modal from exposing emails until approval is granted.

ashok: Implementation notes for eng-platform: add new fields to audit event store, but do NOT index actor_email by default to avoid accidental leaks. Index actor_hash, tenant_id, resource_id, event_type, timestamp, and affected_paths.

ida: How about routing metadata? We should include `effective_routing_snapshot` (small condensed view) so investigators can see the route decision context without replaying the whole evaluation pipeline.

jordan: Make it optional and size-limited (e.g., 4kb). If evaluation trace > 4kb include `trace_summary` and link to full trace only accessible in Dedicated/Private with proper auth.

sam: Backward compatibility: bump `schema_version` to 2 when we flip actor_email optional field and affected_paths. Provide migration docs and a compatibility layer for old exports (schema_v1 -> rewrite to new fields with nulls).

maria: Ops asks for throttle controls on export generation. Running full-tenant exports is expensive. Let's have rate limits per org and an admin queue with priority levels.

ashok: We'll add an `export_quota` per tenant and an admin emergency bypass with explicit audit record (who used bypass, justify). The export API should return cost_estimate and ETA before generation.

ida: Example export request (POST) that Console would call: 

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/audit/exports \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"tenant_id":"acct_123","filters":{"resource_id":"policy_x97","since":"2024-11-20T00:00:00Z"},"include":{"actor_email":true,"full_snapshot":false},"notify":"sec@redwood.ai"}'
```

jordan: Response idea: 202 Accepted plus `{ "export_id":"exp_678", "cost_estimate":"12MB", "eta":"2024-11-20T18:15:00Z" }` and stream URL when ready.

maria: One more: add `redaction_level` parameter: `none`, `pii_masked`, `pii_removed`. Default `pii_masked` for hosted. Dedicated/Private can opt for `none` after approval.

ashok: Summarizing action items: add fields to event schema (`actor_*`, `affected_paths`, `change_delta`, `schema_version`), stream export resume tokens, export quotas + bypass audit, console export modal + approval flow, and update docs + migration notes. I'll carve tickets.

sam: Thanks — can someone open the RFC PR with examples and security checklist? I can review.

maria: I'll open the PR and ping security + legal.

security-bot: Automated check: when PR is opened include `sec_checklist.md` with encryption, retention, and access control steps.

ashok: Great. Closing loop — we won't surface raw emails in default hosted exports. Anything else?

ida: Maybe add a small retention tag per-event so exports can be filtered by retention policy when exporting. That helps compliance teams.

ashok: Added to the ticket. Thanks all. :party_popper:
